content.value_statement: Swift 6.2 concurrency diagnostics can be hard to connect to actor isolation and Sendable rules. This skill guides focused reviews and minimal fixes for Swift and SwiftUI code.
actual_capabilities: Triage Swift concurrency compiler diagnostics and identify affected symbols.
Explain actor isolation choices for @MainActor, actor, and nonisolated code.
Suggest minimal fixes for Sendable errors and shared mutable state.
Apply Swift 6.2 approachable concurrency guidance when project settings support it.
Review SwiftUI closures that may run outside the main actor.
limitations: Requires the user to provide code, diagnostics, or project concurrency settings.
Does not run Xcode builds or verify compiler output by itself.
Cannot prove thread safety without enough context about shared mutable state.
Guidance targets Swift 6.2+ and may need adjustment for older Swift versions.

use_cases.title: Fix Compiler Errors
use_cases.description: An iOS developer maps Swift concurrency diagnostics to the smallest actor isolation or Sendable change.

use_cases.title: Plan Swift 6 Migration
use_cases.description: An engineering lead reviews project settings and migration risks before enabling stricter concurrency checks.

use_cases.title: Review SwiftUI Responsiveness
use_cases.description: A SwiftUI engineer checks closures, async tasks, and background work for data-race safety and smooth UI updates.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Diagnostic
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Swift concurrency diagnostic in simple terms. Identify the actor isolation issue and suggest the smallest safe fix: [paste diagnostic and code].

prompt_templates.title: Fix a File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Swift file for Swift 6.2 concurrency issues. Propose minimal edits for @MainActor, Sendable, nonisolated, and actor boundaries: [paste file].

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for approachable concurrency migration. Use these project settings and identify changes that preserve behavior: [settings and files].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Architecture Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this async architecture for data-race safety and responsiveness. Compare actor, @MainActor, @concurrent, and Sendable options: [context].

output_examples.input: A compiler diagnostic says a main actor model sends a mutable helper to a nonisolated async method.
output: Explains the actor boundary that caused the diagnostic.
Recommends keeping UI-owned state on the main actor when behavior should remain serial.
Suggests offloading only the expensive work that must run in parallel.

output_examples.input: A SwiftUI visual effect closure reads an instance property through self.
output: Flags the Sendable closure capture risk.
Recommends capturing the needed value instead of the whole instance.
Explains why the closure may run outside the main actor.

output_examples.input: A team wants to enable Swift 6.2 approachable concurrency for an existing app.
output: Checks default actor isolation and strict concurrency settings.
Identifies UI-bound code that can rely on main actor defaults.
Lists areas that still need explicit actors or Sendable review.

best_practices: Start with the exact compiler diagnostic and the smallest affected code region.
Prefer actor isolation changes that preserve current behavior before adding new concurrency.
State project Swift version and strict concurrency settings in every request.
anti_patterns: Adding @unchecked Sendable without explaining the thread-safety proof.
Moving UI-bound state off the main actor only to satisfy one diagnostic.
Requesting broad rewrites without compiler diagnostics or behavior requirements.

faq.question: What Swift versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Swift 6.2+ concurrency behavior, including approachable concurrency and default actor isolation.

faq.question: Can it fix SwiftUI concurrency warnings?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for SwiftUI actor isolation, Sendable closures, Task usage, and responsive background work.

faq.question: Does it replace compiler checks?
faq.answer: No. You should still build the project and run tests after applying any suggested change.

faq.question: Can it choose between actor and @MainActor?
faq.answer: It can explain tradeoffs and recommend an isolation model based on ownership, UI use, and shared mutable state.

faq.question: Does it use external commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is reference guidance and does not require shell commands.

faq.question: What should I include in a prompt?
faq.answer: Include the diagnostic text, the related Swift code, Swift version, strict concurrency setting, and intended behavior.
